items.abstract: <jats:p>Iterative improvements from feedback is a general approach for many, if not all, successful systems.Ground-truth-in-the-loop is critical.Language models (LMs) like ChatGPT are phenomenal, however, there are still issues like hallucinations and a lack of planning and controllability.We may leverage LMs' competence of language to handle tasks by prompting, fine-tuning, and augmenting with tools and APIs.AI aims for optimality.(Current) LMs are approximations, thus induce an LM-to-real gap. Our aim is to bridge such a gap.Previous study shows that grounding, agency and interaction are the cornerstone for sound and solid LMs.Iterative improvements from feedback is critical for further progress of LMs and reinforcement learning is a promising framework, although pre-training then fine-tuning is a popular approach.Iterative updates are too expensive for monolithic large LMs, thus smaller LMs are desirable.A modular architecture is thus preferred.These help make LMs adapt to humans, but not vice verse.We discuss challenges and opportunities, in particular, data & feedback, methodology, evaluation, interpretability, constraints and intelligence.</jats:p>

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Refine Automatic Feedback Generation at Articulatory Level in Computer Aided Pronunciation Training

items.abstract: A recent trend in computational cognitive science is to use large-scale naturalistic data to evaluate cognitive theories (Griffiths, 2015; Jones, 2017). This article extends this work by examining the connection between social feedback and language usage. Social feedback, operationalized here as the difference between the number of upvotes and downvotes on comments on the social media forum Reddit, provides a unique opportunity to investigate how social approval interacts with linguistic behavior. To accomplish this, social feedback ratings from over 400 billion words of comments from the social media forum Reddit were mined. Two types of corpora were formed: 1) large (approximately 1.7 billion words) combined corpora of positive, negative, and neutral comments, and 2) individual corpora from over 1,500 high-level commenters on Reddit (following recent work by Johns, 2021a, 2023, 2024a,b using individualized language models). Both were used to examine social feedback and language usage across multiple sets of lexical organization and lexical semantic data with distributional modeling techniques. It was found that comments that receive positive social feedback tended to align more closely with normative language usage, suggesting that the acceptability of a communicative message may lie in the form of that utterance and not just the content of it. Additionally, this trend was replicated at the individual level, where commenters who had more normative usage of language generally received more positive ratings on their comments.
title: Large-scale social feedback and language usage: A distributional analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>With the growing global interest in language learning driven by cross-cultural communication and online education, the need for scalable language immersion remains unmet. This study investigates how large language models (LLMs) can enhance access to quality language learning, specifically pronunciation guidance, by replicating key aspects of human tutoring. We propose an AI-powered pronunciation training system that utilizes LLMs for real-time phonetic transcription and contextualized feedback in order to democratize immersion learning for language learners. Results from a small-scale evaluation of the LLM feedback based on a seven-category rubric indicated the system's clear feedback and excellent motivational quality, while noting areas for improvement in dialect sensitivity. These findings suggest that integrating LLMs with user-friendly interfaces can provide a viable source of simulated immersion learning for a larger range of learners.</jats:p>
title: Democratizing Pronunciation Training through Large Language Models

project-title.title: Use of Large Language Models to Scale Training for Rheumatic Heart Disease Screening Among Primary Care Nurses in Uganda

project-description.description:
Statement of Need: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is the most common acquired cardiovascular disease among young people worldwide. Secondary antibiotic prophylaxis can prevent disease progression, but its uptake remains sub-optimal. One major barrier is low RHD detection rates, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where only 1-2% of people who have RHD are diagnosed. A scalable, replicable approach to build and maintain echocardiographic (echo) capacity for a decentralized RHD screening workforce is urgently needed to improve RHD detection rates.
Organizational Background: The RHD Research Collaborative in Uganda (RRCU), co-founded by Dr. Beaton (primary mentor) and Dr. Okello (co-mentor) is a network of clinician scientists working to reduce the global burden of RHD. One RRCU project, ADUNU, is partnering with the Ugandan Ministry of Health to develop a model for decentralized RHD services integrated into the primary healthcare structure of Uganda. ADUNU builds on a decade of RRCU research showing that echo screening is the best tool for early RHD detection, and that it can be task-shifted to nurses and integrated into routine care. In collaboration with the REAN Foundation, this application seeks to develop a replicable, technology-empowered model to scale-up echo training for RHD screening. 
Project Goals: The overall objective of this application is to co-create and test a large language model (LLM)-based WhatsApp “bot” to provide interactive, just in time content to maximize the effectiveness and efficiency of nurse echo training. We will utilize human-centered design to co-create a bot that is contextually and culturally appropriate and tailored to user needs. We will then study barriers and facilitators to adoption, including measures of acceptability, feasibility, appropriateness, and engagement. Lastly, we will compare performance outcomes between STANDARD and ENHANCED training including results of knowledge-based assessment, screening accuracy, and frequency of specific errors.  
Budget: In addition to post-doctoral salary support, our budget includes $3,000 for statistics, regulatory, and travel. Other costs will be supported through the ADUNU parent grant and Dr. Beaton’s lab.
